'''Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel''' (born 1982)<ref name=mphd/> is a [[Turkish-American]] [[statistician]]<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> and professor of the practice at [[Duke University]], and a professional educator at [[RStudio]]. She is the author of several open source statistics textbooks<ref name=r4ds/><ref name=intro/><ref name=open/><ref name=high/> and is an instructor for [[Coursera]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.coursera.org/instructor/minecetinkayarundel |title=Coursera Instructor Profile: Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel |publisher=Coursera |access-date=2017-10-30 |archive-date=2018-03-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309200349/https://www.coursera.org/instructor/minecetinkayarundel |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2016/12/online-education-a-complicated-history-at-duke|title=Coursera connections: Examining online education at Duke|publisher=The Chronicle|access-date=2017-10-30|archive-date=2017-10-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029040527/http://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2016/12/online-education-a-complicated-history-at-duke|url-status=live}}</ref> She is the chair-elect of the Statistical Education Section of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://community.amstat.org/statisticaleducationsection/aboutus/officers|title=Statistical Education Section Officers|publisher=American Statistical Association|access-date=2017-10-30|archive-date=2017-09-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902024218/http://community.amstat.org/statisticaleducationsection/aboutus/officers|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=off>{{Official URL}}</ref> Previously, she was a senior lecturer at [[University of Edinburgh]].

==Education==
Çetinkaya-Rundel grew up in [[Turkey]] and graduated from [[Robert College]],<ref name="ClassCentral">{{cite web |url=https://www.class-central.com/report/duke-coursera-data-analysis-and-statistical-inference/ |title=A Passion for Stats and the Beauty of Bayes: A Duke Professor on Teaching Online |work=Class Central's MOOC Report |publisher=Class Central |date=2015-03-24 |access-date=2017-10-30 |archive-date=2016-03-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322213127/https://www.class-central.com/report/duke-coursera-data-analysis-and-statistical-inference/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  before coming to the United States for her undergraduate studies to study actuarial science at [[New York University]]. After working as an [[actuary]] at [[Buck Consultants]],<ref name=mphd/> Çetinkaya-Rundel enrolled in graduate school at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]. She earned her master's degree and PhD in statistics at UCLA where her dissertation on estimating the impact of [[air pollution]]<ref name=mphd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Mine|last=C̜etinkaya |title=Estimating the impact of air pollution using small area estimation |publisher=University of California, Los Angeles |date=2011 |url=http://publications.stat.ucla.edu/dissertations/single-page/?smid=274|website=ucla.edu|id={{ProQuest|920151211}} |oclc= 781649608}}</ref> was supervised of [[Jan de Leeuw]].<ref name=mathgene>{{mathgenealogy}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Çetinkaya-Rundel coauthored three open-access textbooks, ''[[OpenIntro Statistics]]'',<ref name=aphelo>{{cite journal|last=Aphalo|first=Pedro José|date=February 2017|doi=10.19232/uv4pb.2016.2.90|journal=UV4Plants Bulletin|pages=51–53|title=Review of ''OpenIntro Statistics''|volume=2|issue=2}}</ref> ''Introductory Statistics with Randomization and Simulation'', and ''OpenIntro: Advanced High School Statistics''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.openintro.org/stat/textbook.php?stat_book=isrs|title=Introductory Statistics with Randomization and Simulation|publisher=OpenIntro|access-date=2017-10-30|archive-date=2018-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101030147/https://www.openintro.org/stat/textbook.php?stat_book=isrs|url-status=live}}</ref> She is an author on the associated [[R (programming language)|R package]], openintro.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/openintro/index.html|title=openintro Data Sets and Supplemental Functions from 'OpenIntro' Textbooks|publisher=CRAN|date=2017-09-08|access-date=2017-10-30|archive-date=2018-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101030016/https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/openintro/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Çetinkaya-Rundel is also a proponent of reproducible analysis<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.science20.com/news_articles/scientific_reproducibility_it_going_extinct_or_do_we_not_teach_statistics_well_enough-130760|title=Scientific Reproducibility - Is It Going Extinct Or Do We Not Teach Statistics Well Enough?|publisher=Science 2.0|date=2014-02-28|access-date=2017-10-30|archive-date=2018-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101030131/http://www.science20.com/news_articles/scientific_reproducibility_it_going_extinct_or_do_we_not_teach_statistics_well_enough-130760|url-status=live}}</ref> in the context of statistics education.<ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=1402.1894|title=R Markdown: Integrating A Reproducible Analysis Tool into Introductory Statistics |journal=Technology Innovations in Statistics Education |volume=8 |issue=1 |last1=Baumer |first1=Ben |last2=Cetinkaya-Rundel |first2=Mine |last3=Bray |first3=Andrew |last4=Loi |first4=Linda |last5=Horton |first5=Nicholas J |year=2014 |doi=10.5070/T581020118  |doi-access=free|bibcode=2014arXiv1402.1894B }}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Çetinkaya-Rundel was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA) in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|title=ASA Fellows list|publisher=American Statistical Association|access-date=2020-06-01|archive-date=2019-04-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425013824/https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> She was elected chair of the ASA Statistical Computing program in 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|title=2021 ASA Election Results|url=https://www.amstat.org/asa/files/pdfs/2021-ASAElectionResults.pdf}}</ref>
